blog_posts.title: The Complete Restaurant SEO Guide for 2024
blog_posts.excerpt: How Noida restaurants can dominate Google Maps and Zomato search with a locality-first SEO strategy.
blog_posts.content:
Restaurant SEO is fundamentally different from standard SEO. Your customers are searching within a 3–5 km radius, they're hungry right now, and they're comparing you against 10 other listings simultaneously.

**1. Own your Google Business Profile**

Your GBP is the single most important real estate in local search. Fill every field, add photos weekly, respond to every review within 24 hours.

**2. Build review velocity, not just review count**

Google's local algorithm rewards recency. 50 reviews from last month beat 500 reviews from 3 years ago.

**3. Menu-led keyword strategy**

Your menu items are your keywords. 'Butter chicken near me', 'best biryani in Noida Sector 18' — these are real queries your customers type.

**4. Zomato & Swiggy listing optimisation**

Your delivery platform listing is a search engine too. Photos, descriptions, and response time all affect your ranking.

blog_posts.title: The D2C Product Launch Playbook: From Zero to ₹10L/Month
blog_posts.excerpt: A step-by-step framework for launching a D2C product brand in India — from pre-launch to month 3 and beyond.
blog_posts.content:
Launching a D2C product in India has never been more accessible — or more competitive.

**Pre-Launch (8 weeks before)**

Build your audience before you have a product to sell. Start content on Instagram and YouTube. Run a waitlist campaign.

**Launch Week**

Don't launch on all channels simultaneously. Start with your own D2C site and one marketplace.

**Month 1: Data over everything**

The first month is about learning, not scaling. Which product variant sells? Which ad creative wins?

**Month 2–3: Scale what works**

Once you have data, double down. Scale the winning ad creative and expand to the next marketplace.

blog_posts.title: Google Maps Ranking Factors for Local Businesses in 2024
blog_posts.excerpt: The three pillars of Google Maps ranking — relevance, distance, and prominence — and how to optimise each one.
blog_posts.content:
Google Maps uses three core factors to rank local businesses: relevance, distance, and prominence.

**Relevance**

How well does your business match the search query? This is influenced by your business category, GBP description, and the keywords in your reviews.

**Distance**

How close is your business to the searcher? You can expand your relevance radius by targeting location-specific keywords.

**Prominence**

How well-known is your business? This is determined by your review count and rating, photos, and overall online presence.
